recipes.name: Baked Fish with Shrimp
ingredients_raw: 0.5 pound cooked medium shrimp, peeled and deveined

steps.text: Preheat oven to 325 degrees F (165 degrees C).

In a small saucepan, melt butter over medium low heat. Whisk in flour and salt to make a paste. Gradually whisk in milk. Stirring constantly, cook until sauce is thick enough to coat the back of a spoon.
Select a pan large enough to accommodate all the fillets in one layer. Coat with cooking spray. Arrange fish in pan, and cover with shrimp.. Pour white sauce over shrimp. Sprinkle with grated cheese.

raw_recipe.headline: Baked Fish with Shrimp
raw_recipe.description: Easy and delicious way to impress your family and guests with a recipe that's almost too simple! The fillets are covered with cooked shrimp and a simple white sauce. Grated Parmesan cheese is sprinkled over the top of this baked dish. Grouper, snapper, and catfish are all good choices for this recipe.

review.reviewBody:
This was absolutely delicious, easy to make & better than any fish I have had in restaurants. First of all I couldn't get snapper so I used Kingclip fillets which I had never had before, very fishy smelling but not fishy in taste. Fillets were pretty thick so had to add a little more cooking time. I did as some others suggested and added a few seasonings. I added a little sliced onion, garlic salt, salt &cracked pepper, 
bay seasoning & 4 Tbls. sherry. I used a half pound of med. cooked shrimp & removed the shell on the tails before I put on fish. Really thought they would be tough as they were already cooked with the cooking in the oven besides but they were just find, not at all tough or dry. This dish is definately a keeper, also can easily be prepared a little ahead of time if having company, get your other sides in order & ready to cook, sit back & enjoy your company with a little drink & just pop it in the oven when ready to cook. I am not a big fish lover but this was excellent & certainly deserves a 5 Star in my opinion.

Made this with tilapia fillets and shrimp. Using this recipe as a base and some reviewers tips, the finished product was beyond yummy. I only had 3/4c of milk on hand and used heavy cream to make a full cup - having just a bit of heavy cream left in the container I added it and it totaled 1 1/4cup. I added 8 sliced cloves of garlic 4 tbsp of butter as it was melting. To the 2tbsp of flour I added 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp black pepper, 1/2 tsp emerald essence (substitution for old bay seasoning) 1/2 tsp mural of flavor (which is basically a blend of a dozen different herbs without salt - purchased from Penzeys spices). I added 20 shrimp to boiling water and cooked for 2 minutes and drained. I put all the fish in the pan as instructed and grated 1/4c of fresh parmiggiano-regiano cheese over everyting. Cooked it for 30 minutes in a preheated 350 degree oven. Fantastic!

Oh my goodness! Fabulous. I used red snapper, cooked shrimp and added sea scallops. I also added lemon juice, old bay, minced garlic and sherry to the sauce. I rubbed the snapper with salt, pepper and a bit of old bay. I will make this again and again and again. I forgot to add that I sprinkle parm grated cheese over scallops, shrimp before pouring sauce over casserole dish then after sauce sprinkled fresh parm shredded cheese over the top of the dish. Thank you MLT for sharing such a marvelous recipe!!

I left off the shrimp because all I wanted was a fish recipe to use up some red snapper I had in the freezer. I followed the suggestions of some other reviewers and added some pressed garlic and rehydrated dried onion flakes to the butter before adding the flour. I also added a splash of sherry to the finished white sauce. I only had one pound of fish (there are only 2 of us) and since it is over 100 here in Las Vegas, I baked the fish in the toaster oven so as not to heat up the kitchen too much. I sprinkled some paprika on the sauce-covered fish before adding the cheese, and placed a couple of thin lemon slices on each fillet along with a sprig of thyme before baking. This come out delicious and my husband really liked it! Exactly what I was looking for. Thanks!

Personal preference omitted the cheese.
Substituted 1/4 tsp lower sodium chicken 'Better than Bouillion' for the salt.
For 2 people and 2 large fillets, I used a generous 1/4 lb of small cooked Oregon Shrimp.
Sauteed 1 large minced garlic clove while melting the butter, and added 3 thin sliced green onions to the completed sauce.
I will make it again and again, easy, elegant, tasty.

I used cod and uncooked shrimp with the seasonings that we like with our seafood, garlic, sherry and fresh parsley. I covered the cast iron skillet for 15 mins and removed the cover the last 5 mins. It was good but, without using cooking common sense and adding preferred spices, it would've been too bland for our taste buds, thus 4 stars instead of 5. Oh and for the milk, I always mix evaporated in for the extra creamy texture. I think I will add lump crab the next time I make it, and I will be making it again and again.

Loved it! Very delicious and easy to make. Served over garlic mashed potatoes with a side of steamed vegetables. Modified the recipe with the following as suggested by others: Used frozen tilapia and frozen precooked shrimp. Thawed both under fresh water, patted dry, and placed in large casserole dish. Seasoned both with Tony Chacere's Creole seasoning salt, McCormicks Gourmet Roasted Coriander, McCormicks Gourmet Moroccan Seasoning. Added minced garlic to the butter before adding the flour, and added about a 1/2 cup of Sherry Cooking Wine, and just a pinch of salt. Used fresh grated Parmesan cheese thick layer, and sprinkled the top with a small amount of cayenne, and more of the Moroccan seasoning for color. Because I used a large casserole dish I had to increase the time cooked to 35-40 minutes. Best if served immediately from the oven. Awesome!

I made this with sole instead of snapper. And used 1/2lb raw prawns and left over Trader Joe canned dungenous crabmeat. Added some old bay seasoning to the sauce when salt was added. I baked it for 28 minutes since the prawns were raw and the sole 1/2 thawed. Served over bed of Dreamfields angel hair pasta. It was so good and my family loved it! Per my son, "Creamy deliciousness!" Next time I would add more old bay seasoning and perhaps garlic powder and other herbs to season up the sauce more. This is a keeper.

I really liked this recipe just like others I did add a little bit of extra ingredients. First I made it exactly the way the recipes calls for but I added 1 extra tablespoon of butter to the sauce. Once I did that I tasted and I felt like it could use a little more of something. So I added some minced garlic probably about 1 tsp of minced garlic, dash of pepper and it made the sauce soooo much better. Instead of red snapper, I used seasoned catfish and tilapia the catfish is much better but the tilapia is good as well. I will definitely be making this again for so many people.

This is definitely a winner in our house. But to spruce it up, I added semi cooked onions and sliced red bell pepper on top of the fish before adding the sauce. I also mixed bread crumbs and parmesan cheese to the top the last 15 minutes to make a slight crust on top. I would have given it five stars if I hadn’t messed with the recipe.

Just made this, excellent!! Added 2T white wine, seasoning salt, garlic and dried onion to the sauce. Lightly cooked my shrimp in garlic butter first. (Had raw frozen jumbo shrimp, also cut them in half)Used fresh snapper. Placed on a bed of quinoa with some steamed green beans on the side. Will definately make this again and again!!

As written, I agree with other reviewers that this might be kind of bland as I tried the sauce before adding anything. I added some grated garlic and smoked paprika. Instead of salt, I used some cajun seasoning. I will definitely be making this again!

Made some changes, due to availability of items. Used tilapia filets. Started with a mixture of olive oil and butter, added fresh chopped garlic and onions. Also had some leftover ham from New Year’s (Georgia girl). Added my herbs while frying (Old Bay, garlic, onion, salt, pepper, paprika). Then shoved in the shrimp and cooked. Removed each and placed on top of leftover cooked spaghetti noodles and tilapia in a casserole dish. Put Parmesan and mozzarella on top. Added flour to make a roux with the leftover oils and spices in the pan. Then added Sake (no white wine) and half and half. Poured it over the tilapia, shrimp annd noodles in the pan and baked at 325 for approx 30 mins.
top dish simple and tasty having it again tonight
It was awful. Pasty and bland. I used haddock and sauteed the shrimp in butter and garlic - the shrimp wasn't too bad if it didn't have much of the pasty rue on it.

This is such a great recipe! I always add some seasoned spinach on the plate first then add the fish and shrimp on top. My whole family loves this and I feel it's better than any restaurant would serve.
I seasoned the sauce and added red hot peppers.
Great recipe. I added some other ingredients; minced garlic, smoked gouda cheese, topped with crab meat, then added panko towards the end of baking until golden brown. Fantastic!

This was really good! I did add some garlic & salted the fish. If anyone else wonders about using raw shrimp, yes it works fine. I cut them in pieces b/c they were large. Just make sure to thoroughly thaw & dry fish & shrimp.
Agree better then any restaurant I’ve ever had did the same added seasoning to fish before and to sauce instant favorite
